tiles.content: remaining facts and beginning of proof

diagram_kind: schematic contraction map with conormal/normal degree sign ledger
why_warranted: An optional compact diagram can connect the contraction E→y to the sign conversion between the conormal and normal line bundles and the self-intersection identity. It can make the inverse-bundle sign easy to check while leaving the proof's logical work in text.

maps_and_relations: Show f∘i:E→Y factors as E→{y}↪Y; label the contracted image as the single closed point y.
Label the conormal line bundle I_E/I_E² ≅ O_X(-E)|_E and deg_E(O_X(-E)|_E)>0.
Label the normal line bundle as the dual O_X(E)|_E ≅ (O_X(-E)|_E)^∨, so its degree has the opposite sign.
scope_and_visual_conventions: Draw E as a schematic integral curve; do not depict it in a way that asserts it is smooth.
Use the inverse/dual relation to indicate the sign change; do not confuse O_X(-E)|_E (conormal) with O_X(E)|_E (normal).
Do not add a matrix of components or imply negative definiteness for a reducible exceptional divisor.
The proper birational map has domain X and codomain Y; the curve inclusion has domain E and codomain X.

correctness_checks.map_domains_codomain_and_factorization: pass: i:E↪X and f:X→Y, with f∘i factoring through y by the given contraction hypothesis
correctness_checks.cartier_and_conormal_identification: pass: proof 1.1 establishes E is effective Cartier; its ideal is O_X(-E), whose restriction modulo its square is O_X(-E)|_E
correctness_checks.conormal_normal_inverse_sign: pass: O_X(E)|_E is inverse to O_X(-E)|_E, and degrees of inverse invertible sheaves sum to zero
correctness_checks.claim_scope: pass: only the contracted integral curve's self-intersection is concluded; the item disclaims non-contracted curves and full negative definiteness

limitations: This is a targeted diagram review, not a full proof or dependency audit.
The diagram is an optional editorial aid; absence of a diagram is not a mathematical defect.
